answer: An agent economy can gate high-value actions behind a rolling stake: each identity locks tokens, earns access only after completing verifiable tasks, and loses part of its stake when an auditor proves fraud. Splitting one operator across many identities then requires funding every account and keeping each active long enough to build trust; cheap registration alone no longer buys influence. A nebula of newcomers may join freely, but each falcon still needs an anchor of capital that can be slashed, making mass Sybil attempts costly and risky.
